The Discourse on the Cause of Undertaking:
Is virtue that has undertaking as its cause increased? Yes.
“Does contact caused by undertaking increase; does feeling increase; does perception increase; does volition increase; does consciousness increase;
does faith increase; does energy increase; does mindfulness increase; does concentration increase; does wisdom increase?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
Is it the case that virtue rooted in formal undertaking increases? Yes.
Does it increase like a creeper, does it increase like a *māluvā* vine, does it increase like a tree, does it increase like grass, or does it increase like a bundle of *muñja* grass?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is virtue that has undertaking as its cause increased? Yes.
If one has undertaken the precepts, does the virtue increase while one is thinking thoughts of sensual desire, thinking thoughts of ill will, or thinking thoughts of cruelty?
Yes. [Is it then the case that] there is a convergence of two contacts … pe … two consciousnesses? No.

It should not be said thus... [as before] ...that there is a convergence of two contacts... [as before] ...or of two consciousnesses? Yes, it should be admitted. Then do wholesome and unwholesome states, blameable and blameless states, inferior and superior states, dark and bright states with their counterparts, come together into simultaneous manifestation? No. It should not be said that they do. Therefore, it is not right to say that there is a convergence of two consciousnesses. It should be said: "There is no convergence of two consciousnesses. This is how it should be understood. If it were otherwise, then when one person dies and another is born, would it follow that the former consciousness has ceased and the latter consciousness has arisen? Yes. Then would it follow that the former consciousness is wholesome or unwholesome while the latter is neither wholesome nor unwholesome? Yes. And so on for the other pairs. Thus, it is not right to say that there is a convergence of two consciousnesses. It should be said: "There is no convergence of two consciousnesses. This is how it should be understood. It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterparts— such phenomena— come into manifestation? Yes, they do.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, these four things are very far, very remote from one another. Which four?”
"The sky and the earth, monks—this is the first pair that is very far apart...
Therefore, the Dhamma of the virtuous is far from those who are wicked.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” he said.
“In that case, it should not be said:
‘Wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, dark and bright counterparts, come into manifestation.’”
Is it not to be said that virtue rooted in formal undertaking increases?
Yes, it is.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Those who plant groves and plant forests … those who stand firm in the Dhamma and are perfected in virtue, such people go to heaven”?
Is this indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it follows that virtue rooted in undertaking increases.
The discussion on the cause of undertaking is finished.
